cannotProve.label: Cannot prove
cannotProve.fallback: A number on its own cannot show why it moved.

gate.final: This cycle is in its last phase. Write the 90-day review below, then start a new cycle from the goal's page.

evidence.gone: The record this pointed at no longer exists

home.title: Learning loop
home.lead: One goal at a time, in cycles of ninety days. Each phase opens only on evidence (answers, notes and reviews the product already recorded), and every number here says what it cannot show.
home.nothingDue: Nothing from your mastery paths is waiting right now.

start.scenarioHint: A real situation, not a topic: the meeting, the exam, the conversation.
start.outcome: What you can do in twelve weeks
start.outcomeHint: Something someone else could watch you do.
start.taskHint: Small enough to do this week, even on a bad week.

week.cannotProve: A scored week shows you looked back at it. It cannot show that next week will go better.

state.minimumHint: The smallest version that still counts. "I got interrupted" switches to it.
state.boundariesHint: One per line. A resumed chat is told these; AnyTools cannot enforce them.
state.handoverHint: What a fresh conversation should start from. A resumed chat's update can replace it once it passes the check below.
state.noHypotheses: Nothing yet. Writing back a weekly review adds its mistakes and its one change here.

interrupt.title: Interrupted
interrupt.lead: If this week fell apart, shrink the plan instead of dropping it: the next task becomes its minimum version, and the interruption is logged on the cycle.
interrupt.minimum: Smallest version of your next task

resume.title: Resume with AI
resume.lead: Opens a new chat that is shown this goal and nothing else. It restates it, runs one short exercise, and ends with an update you can bring back here.
resume.takeNextTask: Also take its suggested next task
resume.accepted: Accepted. The handover note is updated.
resume.valid: This update passes the check and can be accepted.

chain.title: Evidence chains
chain.question: A question to follow over time

brief.title: AI task briefs
brief.task: A task you will hand to AI
brief.outputEval: How the output will be judged
brief.cost: Cost, and how easy it is to undo
brief.rollback: If it goes wrong, how to roll back
brief.handover: How the work comes back to you
brief.dataNoteHint: The data boundary is a reminder for you. AnyTools cannot control what a model provider does with what you send it.
brief.notReady: Some of the before-you-start checks are not ticked yet.

check.output_eval_written: I know how I will judge the output
check.human_gates_named: I have named where I must sign off
check.rollback_known: I know how to undo it
check.baseline_recorded: I did or measured it once without AI first

review.title: Week {{week}} review
review.noEvidence: Nothing attached yet. Accept a suggestion below, or add one.
review.suggestedLead: Things you did in this week of the cycle. Nothing counts until you add it; a nightly pass also proposes these for you to accept or dismiss.
review.noSuggestions: Nothing recorded this week yet. Answer a quiz question or write a note, and it will show up here.
review.qualityHint: Was it done well enough to count, by your own bar?
review.retentionHint: Could you still do last week's material without help?
review.transferHint: Did you use it anywhere other than where you learned it?
review.mistakesHint: Each one you fill in becomes a hypothesis on the goal when you write the review back.
review.change: One thing to change next week
review.changeHint: One. Changing several at once makes next week impossible to read.
review.done: Written back. Its mistakes and its change are now hypotheses on the goal, and the review is frozen.
review.ready: Complete. Writing it back adds its mistakes and its change to the goal's hypotheses.

chainPage.interpretation: What you take it to mean

log.title: AI learning logs
log.lead: Measure the same task three times: without AI, with AI, and alone again a few days later. Only the third run can show what you kept.

cards.title: Evidence cards
cards.lead: A card follows one skill in one real situation: an attempt made without help, practice, a retest after a delay, and the same skill somewhere new.
cards.none: No evidence cards on this goal yet.
cards.cardTitle: A short name for this card
cards.hidden: Your first attempt is hidden until the retest is saved, so it cannot cue your answer.
cards.retestOpensOn: The retest opens on {{date}}. Until then, practise; the first attempt stays hidden.
cards.retestOpen: The retest is open. Answer from memory, then say how much help you had.
cards.transferWaits: Record a transfer once the retest is saved.
cards.writeHint: Up to 20,000 characters. It is kept exactly as you save it and cannot be edited later.
cards.baselineWarning: Save only what you did without help. If you already looked something up, save it as practice instead.
cards.promptLevel: How much help did you have?
cards.linkDocument: A document page: paste its address
cards.linkDocumentHint: For example /documents/…?page=3, copied from the reader.
cards.linkMissing: This link points at something that no longer exists.

reflect.intro: Close the card when you are done with it. No more entries can be added afterwards.

cards.cannotProve: A retest on one card shows the skill lasted once, in one situation. It cannot show it will hold under pressure or in a different kind of task.

contract.title: Minimum contract for bad days
contract.lead: Answer these on an ordinary day, so a bad one has nothing left to decide. Shrinking a task is not dodging it: when health, money, safety or the people close to you are at real risk, pausing and asking for help can be the most responsible move for the long run.
contract.downshift: When do I shrink the task instead of pushing through?
contract.downshiftHint: The signs that pushing would cost more than it gives, such as too little sleep, a deadline at work, or a third failed try.
contract.keep: After shrinking it, what small action is still worth keeping?
contract.keepHint: The minimum version above is the task itself. Say why it is worth keeping, or what else is.
contract.help: When do I ask for help, or hand this to someone qualified?
contract.helpHint: Who you would turn to, and what would make you do it.
contract.shared: Your first two answers are included when you resume this goal in a chat with your own AI model. The third is never sent to any model; only you see it here.

interruption.lead: If this week fell apart, shrink the plan instead of dropping it. Write down what happened, then what is left: the next task becomes the reduced one, and the record is kept on the cycle.
interruption.factHint: What changed, not a verdict on yourself.
interruption.reducedToHint: This becomes your next task, and its minimum version.
interruption.within24h: Smallest output you can still make within 24 hours
interruption.notRepaying: Work I will not make up
interruption.notRepayingHint: Missed work you are deliberately letting go of, so it does not pile up.
interruption.earlier: Recorded before the six lines existed.

repeated.title: The same resistance, three times running
repeated.body: Your last three interruptions all named {{resistance}}. That is a pattern in the setup, not a lack of willpower. Change a condition rather than asking yourself for more force: the time box may be unrealistic, the task may need splitting, a boundary may need saying out loud, or you may need more support around you.

today.title: Your next step
today.lowDayHint: Shows only the minimum. It resets at the end of the day, and nothing about it is recorded.

cycleClose.lead: Close the cycle step by step: the day-ninety review, the books on ability, artifact, cost and unknowns, one destination for every result, three lines for the year, the quarterly review, and thirty days of handover.
cycleClose.title: Cycle close: {{goal}}
cycleClose.notYet: Day {{day}} of the cycle. The close opens here on day {{from}}.
cycleClose.notesLead: Your own free notes on this cycle. The close keeps its day-ninety review as its own section.
cycleClose.fromLastLead: Week 1 has no question yet. Start it from a result the last cycle sent on:
cycleClose.gone: That result is no longer offered. Reload the page.

repeatedRecovery: Or work through a recovery reset (private)
